inlines.v: TURN'PIKE, noun [turn and pike.] Strictly, a frame consisting of two bars crossing each other at right angles, and turning on a post or pin, to hinder the passage of breasts, but admitting a person to pass between the arms. 1. A gate set across a road to stop travelers and carriages till toll is paid for keeping the road in repair. 2. A turnpike road. 3. In military affairs, a beam filled with spikes to obstruct passage. TURN'PIKE, verb transitive To form, as a road, in the manner of a turnpike road; to throw the path of a road into a rounded form.
